title: Shlok Sangam v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Sunita Agarwal, J.; Deepak Verma, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed; petitioner relegated to a section 127 appeal against the Executive Engineer's computation of theft-assessment dues.
headnote: A consumer's challenge that the Executive Engineer, while granting three instalments under clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, inflated the total theft-assessment dues is a factual dispute. The remedy is an appeal under section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003; the writ petition is dismissed.
facts: The petitioner, Shlok Sangam, challenged the Executive Engineer's assessment of alleged electricity theft. In an earlier writ (Writ-C No. 6869) he had attacked a recovery certificate dated 16 December 2019 seeking instalment payment; the Court directed that request to be considered in accordance with law. The Executive Engineer, Vidyut Vitran Khand-III, Azamgarh, then permitted three instalments under clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. He returned alleging that, in computing those instalments, the total demand had been increased exorbitantly.

holding_units.holding: Where the live grievance is that the Executive Engineer, in computing dues payable in clause 6.14 instalments, has increased the total theft-assessment amount, the dispute is factual and an appeal under section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003 lies to challenge that calculation; the writ petition is dismissed.

principle_tags.application: The Court refused writ interference with the Executive Engineer's computation of theft dues and left the petitioner to a section 127 appeal.
The matter being theft of electricity and the challenge being to the Executive Engineer's assessment computation, the writ was dismissed in favour of the statutory appeal.
Counsel's written instructions established theft of electricity; the Court treated the assessment computation as appealable under section 127.

not_decided.point: Whether the Executive Engineer exorbitantly increased the total theft-assessment dues while computing clause 6.14 instalments
not_decided.note: Left to a section 127 appeal as a factual dispute on calculation.
